title: The Constitution & founding
examples: What was the main problem with the Articles of Confederation?
How did the compromises help create the Constitution?
Can you explain the difference between the Articles and the Constitution?

explain.say: The Articles of Confederation was the first government structure. It was created after the American Revolution.

draw.text: Articles of Confederation: First US Govt.

explain.say: A key weakness was that the central government was too weak. It could not tax the states directly.

draw.text: Weak central government; no taxing power.

explain.say: Another problem was that the states had too much power. They often disagreed on big issues.

draw.text: States held too much power; disagreement.

explain.say: The Constitutional Convention needed compromises to move forward. Compromises meant finding middle ground.
The Great Compromise solved the representation debate. It created two houses in Congress.

draw.text: Great Compromise: Two houses of Congress.

explain.say: In real life, when planning a big event, you must compromise. You might agree on a time that suits everyone.

draw.text: Real life: Agreeing on a time.

faq.q: Why did the Articles of Confederation fail?
faq.a: The main reason was that the national government did not have enough power to manage the country's finances or enforce laws effectively.
asks: What was the biggest weakness of the Articles?
Why couldn't the Articles keep the country together?

faq.q: What was the Great Compromise about?
faq.a: It was a solution to the argument over how many representatives each state would get in the national legislature.
asks: How did they solve the representation problem?
Tell me about the Great Compromise.

faq.q: Did the Constitution fix all the problems?
faq.a: It fixed many major problems, but some issues, like slavery, were left unresolved for later times.
asks: What did the Constitution fail to fix?

faq.q: What is the difference between the Articles and the Constitution?
faq.a: The Constitution created a stronger national government with clearer powers, unlike the Articles.
asks: Can you compare the two documents?

faq.q: Were compromises always easy to reach?
faq.a: No, reaching compromises was very difficult and involved much debate among the delegates.
asks: Was it easy to write the Constitution?
What was the hardest part of the writing?

facts: The Articles of Confederation created a weak central government.
The Great Compromise established a bicameral legislature.
Compromises were necessary to gain agreement among the states.
The Constitution established a stronger federal system.

quiz.say: The Articles of Confederation failed because:

options.show: The King sent armies to take over.
options.say: The King sent armies to take over.

options.show: The people were too busy farming.
options.say: The people were too busy farming.

options.show: The national government could not tax the states directly.
options.say: The national government could not tax the states directly.

options.show: The states refused to join the union.
options.say: The states refused to join the union.

quiz.why: The Articles gave the central government no real power over money.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the American Revolution had already ended.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the main issue was governmental structure.
wrong.3: This is wrong because most states were involved in the initial agreement.

options.show: A council of state leaders only.
options.say: A council of state leaders only.

options.show: A Senate and a House of Representatives.
options.say: A Senate and a House of Representatives.

options.show: A direct election of the President.
options.say: A direct election of the President.

quiz.why: This structure balanced state power with population size.

wrong.0: This would have excluded the voice of the common people.
wrong.2: This would have favored only the larger states.
wrong.3: This was a separate issue from representation in Congress.

quiz.say: If a state wanted more power, they would argue for:

options.show: A system closer to the Articles of Confederation.
options.say: A system closer to the Articles of Confederation.

quiz.why: The Articles favored state autonomy over a strong national body.

wrong.0: This is what the Constitution tried to establish.
wrong.1: The Senate was part of the solution, not the argument for more power.
wrong.2: The goal was self-governance, not rule by a king.
